title: EEG datasets
text:
This page catalogs open EEG data: the places it is published, and the datasets themselves with their rough size. It is a map for finding data, not a benchmark. Every number comes from the dataset’s own page or paper, and a blank means the source doesn’t report it.
Benchmark libraries cover one paradigm family each: 200 of MOABB’s 206 datasets, for example, are BCI paradigms (motor imagery, ERP, SSVEP and c-VEP), and it loads none of the large clinical or sleep corpora. Labs also tend to publish to one repository each, so no single source sees everything. The tables below span EEG repositories, general-purpose repositories, clinical corpora and lab websites.
The catalog is two CSV files in the repo, catalog/sources.csv and catalog/datasets.csv, so you can load, filter or correct it. Each row there also records the license, the reference, the page its numbers came from, and notes on how they were counted, including which numbers are approximate. Numbers were gathered on 3 November 2026.
Access:
Trials counts trials across all subjects and sessions; hours is total recording time. Dataset tables are sorted by number of subjects, and each name links to the dataset’s landing page.

The split holds even inside one benchmark. MOABB’s own table of its 206 datasets puts 54 on Zenodo, 19 of them from French labs such as GIPSA-lab and Inria. It puts 21 on PhysioNet, 20 of which are studies from a single P300 collection, bigP3BCI. All 19 on BNCI Horizon 2020 come from European labs, 8 of them Austrian. Figshare holds 17, OSF 13, and Harvard Dataverse 10, 7 of them from Chinese labs. All 4 on GigaDB come from Korean labs. Only 3 are on OpenNeuro, and 31 name no repository at all.

title: EEG datasets
text:
Where EEG data lives
Three kinds of places publish EEG data. Counts are as each source reported them on 3 November 2026.

EEG-focused repositories and corpora
Repositories and corpora built for neural or clinical data. Counts are of EEG datasets, taken from each source’s API or catalog.





Source
EEG datasets
Subjects
Hours
Access
Python access
Notes




NEMAR
652
35,750
105,150
open
REST API (api.nemar.org/datasets); HTTPS file tree (data.nemar.org); Zarr; EEGDash
Approximate: hours sum total_recording_duration for the 619 of 652 EEG datasets that report it. Mirrors 434 OpenNeuro EEG datasets (‘on’ IDs) and now hosts 218 of its own (‘nm’ IDs, 206 from one uploader), mostly BIDS conversions of BCI, PhysioNet and sleep datasets from other repositories.


OpenNeuro
468
27,369

open
GraphQL API (openneuro.org/crn/graphql); openneuro-py; DataLad; S3
Approximate: 468 of 1,935 readable public datasets list eeg among snapshot modalities, subjects summed per dataset (the API’s modality filter alone missed HBN Release 7); no hours field, but NEMAR’s mirror of 434 of them sums about 77,700 h. BIDS-only, so cognitive and clinical research labs dominate: only 3 of MOABB’s 206 BCI datasets live here.


Brain Data Science Platform (BDSP)
50


mixed
web download after credentialing; per-project tools on GitHub (bdsp-core)
Approximate: 50 of 72 listed projects carry the ‘eeg’ topic, many of them paper data-and-code packages; 43 databases are credentialed or restricted, 5 open. Run by Stanford’s Clinical Data Animation Center with Harvard/MGH/BIDMC: Harvard EEG Database, Human Sleep Project v3.0 (119,234 PSG recordings, 90,166 patients), I-CARE, SPaRCNet.


National Sleep Research Resource (NSRR)
42
50,951

DUA
NSRR Ruby gem; nsrr R package; Luna
Approximate: 42 of 55 listed datasets are tagged Polysomnography, subjects summed from their cards; some are animal studies and some (e.g., HCHS, recorded on an ARES Unicorder) are home sleep tests, so not all have full EEG. Mostly US sleep cohorts and trials (SHHS, MESA, MrOS, CHAT, NCHSDB); the site carries a banner saying it is ‘under review for potential modification’.


Kaggle competitions
37


registration
Kaggle API/CLI
37 competitions match ‘EEG’; the research-tier EEG ones are seizure-detection and seizure-prediction (2014), grasp-and-lift-eeg-detection and inria-bci-challenge (2015), melbourne-university-seizure-prediction (2016) and hms-harmful-brain-activity-classification (2024). Data needs a Kaggle account and accepting each competition’s rules.


BNCI Horizon 2020 database
29
344

open
direct HTTP download; MOABB BNCI loaders
29 of 32 entries carry EEG (others fNIRS or ECoG); the live site timed out today, so counts come from the 2026-10-12 Wayback snapshot. Graz University of Technology contributed 11 of the EEG sets and TU Berlin 8, almost all BCI paradigms.


PhysioNet
29


mixed
REST project list (physionet.org/api/v1/project/published/); wfdb-python; wget
Approximate: 28 databases plus the 2018 Challenge whose metadata mention EEG or polysomnography, after removing 7 false positives; 24 are open, the rest restricted or credentialed. Sleep (Sleep-EDF, CAP, HMC), epilepsy (CHB-MIT, Siena), cardiac arrest (I-CARE) and US BCI data (EEGMMIDB, bigP3BCI); all 21 MOABB datasets sourced here are from US labs.


BBCI BCI Competitions II-IV
16


open
direct download after click-through terms; MOABB and braindecode loaders for some
16 EEG data sets across Competitions II (6), III (7 of 8, one ECoG) and IV (3 of 5, one MEG, one ECoG), from Berlin, Graz, Wadsworth and Tuebingen groups. Still the default BCI benchmarks (IV-2a is BNCI 001-2014); Competition I is hosted at Columbia.


PREDiCT (Patient Repository for EEG Data + Computational Tools)
14


open
direct download links
Approximate: the ‘Number of Patients’ column sums to 570 across 14 task and rest datasets (Parkinson’s, mTBI, depression, OCD, schizophrenia) from the University of New Mexico. PDDL public-domain licence; 64-channel BrainVision or Neuroscan recordings.


Tsinghua University BCI Lab downloads
12


open
direct download
12 datasets, mostly SSVEP (Benchmark, BETA, eldBETA, wearable, 160-target) plus RSVP and collaborative BCI. Copies reappear via Zenodo/Figshare in MOABB (Wang2016, Liu2022EldBETA) and TorchEEG (TSUBenchmark).


Healthy Brain Network (Child Mind Institute)
11
4,140

mixed
NITRC/AWS for raw files; OpenNeuro ds005505-ds005516; EEGDash
Approximate: subjects sum the non-BIDS EEG column of the HBN download table for releases 1.1-11 (the 11 BIDS releases on OpenNeuro hold 3,155). Child Mind Institute’s transdiagnostic paediatric cohort; raw downloads need a NITRC login while the BIDS copies are open.


SJTU BCMI SEED datasets
11


request
none (application form); TorchEEG loaders after download
11 SEED-family datasets (emotion, vigilance, cross-cultural, sleep deprivation, video) from Shanghai Jiao Tong University’s BCMI lab. Access via an application form; TorchEEG ships loaders for SEED, SEED-IV and SEED-V.


TUH EEG Corpus (Temple University Hospital)
7
14,987

DUA
rsync over SSH after approval; braindecode TUH/TUHAbnormal/TUHEvents
Official page lists TUEG v2.0.2 (26,846 recordings, 2002-2017) plus 6 labelled subsets (TUAB, TUAR, TUEP, TUEV, TUSZ, TUSL); the patient count is for TUEG v2.0.0 (14,987 patients, 26,846 sessions, 69,652 recordings) from arXiv 2401.10283. Single-hospital clinical archive; access needs a signed form emailed to NEDC, then SSH-key rsync.


European Epilepsy Database (EPILEPSIAE)
1

45,000
request
none (licensed delivery)
Approximate: hours are a lower bound (‘> 45,000 hours’); 275 annotated patient datasets from over 250 patients (200+ scalp, 60 intracranial) with over 2,500 seizures. Paid licences only (e.g., 2,500 EUR for 25 surface datasets), now sold via Campus Technologies Freiburg.


Harvard Electroencephalography Database
1
109,178

DUA
BDSP download after credentialing; Harvard-EEG-Database-Tools on GitHub
v4.1 (published 2025-02-10): 284,343 clinical EEG studies from 109,178 patients at four sites, with linked EHR. Requires BDSP credentialed status and a signed project DUA; no hours figure given.







General-purpose repositories
Repositories that hold any kind of data and don’t tag EEG reliably. The count is search hits for “EEG”, which overstates how many EEG datasets they hold: Zenodo’s hits even include Germany’s renewable-energy law, which is also abbreviated EEG. Much lab-published BCI data lives here all the same.





Source
Search hits
Access
Notes




Figshare
7,562
open
items of type dataset returned by the API search (search_for=EEG, item_type=3), which includes journal supplementary files. Hosts 17 MOABB datasets, largely Chinese groups (e.g., Tsinghua eldBETA) plus Greek MAMEM and Mexican BCI data.


OSF (Open Science Framework)
2,689
open
public OSF projects matching ‘EEG’ in the SHARE index (cardSearchText=EEG, resourceType=Project; 3,349 with components), many holding code or preregistrations rather than data. Favoured by psychology/ERP labs (ERP CORE) and Korea University’s mobile and 2020-competition BCI sets in MOABB.


Kaggle datasets
1,558
registration
unique results of ‘kaggle datasets list -s EEG’ until pages stopped returning items. Mostly user re-uploads of public datasets (e.g., an OpenNeuro ds002778 copy, SAM40), so check provenance and licence.


Zenodo
1,531
mixed
hits for q=EEG with type=dataset; the query also catches Germany’s renewable-energy law (EEG), and ‘electroencephalography OR electroencephalogram’ gives 421. Largest home of MOABB BCI data (54 of 206), led by French labs such as GIPSA-lab Grenoble (Brain Invaders) and Inria.


Hugging Face Hub
1,001
mixed
datasets whose name matches ‘eeg’, of which 738 are EEGDash mirrors of NEMAR/OpenNeuro data; a further 13 datasets sit under the braindecode org. The remaining ~260 are user uploads of mixed provenance and licence.


Harvard Dataverse
535
mixed
datasets returned by the Search API for q=EEG, type=dataset. 10 MOABB BCI datasets live here, 7 from Chinese groups (Tianjin University, CAS, World Robot Contest) and 2 from Japan.


Mendeley Data
413
open
results attributed to Mendeley Data for query=EEG on its search page (419 across all indexed sources). Elsevier’s repository; its 5 MOABB datasets come from Mexico, Ecuador, Indonesia and Turkey.


NIMH Data Archive (NDA)
278
DUA
collections matching ‘EEG’ in NDA’s search API (80 match ‘electroencephalography’). EEG from NIH-funded mental-health studies (autism, psychosis, depression, adolescent sleep); access needs an institutionally signed Data Use Certification.


IEEE DataPort
213
mixed
results for site search ‘EEG’: 181 standard datasets (subscription), 24 open access, 8 competitions. Mostly single-lab engineering datasets, often from consumer headsets (e.g., the Emotiv-based STEW workload set).


Dryad
157
open
hits for q=EEG in the Dryad search API (60 for ‘electroencephalography’). Journal-linked CC0 deposits, human and animal; few large curated EEG collections.


G-Node GIN
45
open
public repositories matching ‘EEG’ from the GIN API, including forks and DOI copies. Small German/Swiss footprint (MPIB Berlin, USZ Zurich scalp EEG + iEEG, mouse hdEEG).


EBRAINS Knowledge Graph
42
mixed
datasets matching ‘EEG’ (21 tagged electroencephalography; 13 controlled access, 12 free, 9 embargoed, 8 restricted). European Human Brain Project labs, e.g., TMS-EEG perturbational complexity and sEEG/hd-EEG stimulation studies.


Synapse (Sage Bionetworks)
25
mixed
public projects matching ‘EEG’ in the Synapse search API, several unrelated (e.g., mPower). Hosts TD-BRAIN (Brainclinics), BrainLat, HarMNqEEG multinational cross-spectra and FACED; access terms vary by project.


DANDI Archive
23
open
dandisets matching ‘EEG’; mostly animal and intracranial (iEEG/sEEG, single-unit) recordings. DANDI is the BRAIN Initiative’s NWB archive, with little human scalp EEG.


GigaDB
8
open
8 EEG datasets among the 11 hits for ‘EEG’ in the GigaDB search API. Data notes for GigaScience; all 4 MOABB datasets here are Korean (Korea University OpenBMI Lee2019, GIST Cho2017).


UCI Machine Learning Repository
4
open
4 datasets match ‘EEG’ in its API (EEG Database, EEG Eye State, EEG SSVEP signals, BEED epilepsy). Small, old ML-benchmark staples.







Aggregators and loader libraries
Catalogs and Python packages that index or load datasets hosted elsewhere, so their counts overlap with the repositories above.





Source
Kind
Datasets
Subjects
Hours
Notes




EEGDash
aggregator
697
41,083
120,657
Approximate: chart-data API totals (691 of 697 with duration), including 11 HBN ‘mini’ subsets and 11 BDF re-releases of HBN; without them 675 datasets and 37,708 subjects. Indexes NEMAR (653) and OpenNeuro (22) so it inherits their lab mix; the site headline (955 datasets, 137,716 h, all modalities) is slightly ahead of the API (952).


MOABB
loader library
206
4,500

Approximate: subjects summed across the 206 dataset classes in the docs table (develop; last release v1.7.2), and some classes share subjects. Its Repository column: Zenodo 54, PhysioNet 21, BNCI 19, Figshare 17, OSF 13, Harvard Dataverse 10, GitHub 7, Mendeley 5, GigaDB 4, OpenNeuro 3, blank 31.


meagmohit/EEG-Datasets (curated list)
aggregator
67


Curated GitHub list (3,143 stars, last commit 2025-10-17) with 67 numbered entries in 11 paradigm sections plus an unfiltered link dump. A common discovery entry point that mostly points back to the repositories above.


TorchEEG
loader library
21


21 dataset loaders in v1.1.3 (latest, released 2024-12-23), weighted to affective EEG (SEED family, DEAP, DREAMER, AMIGOS, MAHNOB, FACED, MPED) plus sleep (HMC, ISRUC, Sleep-EDFx), BCI and auditory attention (KUL, DTU). Most loaders expect the raw files to be obtained first, several under request-only licences.


braindecode
loader library
11


v2.0.0 (released 2026-11-02) ships 11 named dataset classes (TUH, TUHAbnormal, TUHEvents, SleepPhysionet, SleepPhysionetChallenge2018, CHBMIT, SIENA, NMT, HGD, BNCI2014_001, BCICompetitionIVDataset4) plus MOABBDataset, BIDSDataset and Hugging Face Hub wrappers. Its clinical and sleep coverage complements MOABB’s BCI focus; TUH classes need TUH access.


mne.datasets
loader library
9


MNE 1.13.2’s overview lists 9 datasets with scalp EEG (sample, SPM faces, EEGBCI, mTRF, Kiloword, Sleep PSG, ERP CORE, SSVEP, EyeLink EEG-eyetracking); LIMO is also EEG but not labelled so. Most other fetchers are MEG, OPM, sEEG/ECoG or phantoms; teaching-sized, not benchmarks.

title: temple-of-eeg-decoding
text:
Developer Guide
If you are new to using nbdev here are some useful pointers to get you started.

Install eegtemple in Development mode
# make sure eegtemple package is installed in development mode
$ pip install -e .

# make changes under nbs/ directory
# ...

# compile to have changes apply to eegtemple
$ nbdev_prepare

title: temple-of-eeg-decoding
text:
Usage

Installation
Install latest from the GitHub repository:
$ pip install git+https://github.com/bkowshik/temple-of-eeg-decoding.git
or from pypi
$ pip install eegtemple


Documentation
Documentation can be found hosted on this GitHub repository’s pages. Additionally you can find package manager specific guidelines on pypi.
